findings.title: plot.ipynb 'Coloring by hue' and 'Adding a legend' cells crash on fresh execution (hue list 4 short of 8124 rows)
findings.description: Cells 26 and 29 of docs/tutorials/plot.ipynb build hue as 5 chunks of int(8124/5)=1624 entries (total 8120) for the 8124-row mushrooms dataset. hypertools 1.0's plot() now strictly requires one hue value per observation, so the shipped tutorial crashes on cells that the committed outputs show succeeding (older hypertools tolerated the short list). The tutorial's own markdown states the exact-length rule that its code violates. The library-side error message itself is excellent; the tutorial example is broken.
findings.repro:
cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp
m = hyp.load('mushrooms')
split = int(m.shape[0]/5)
hue = [1]*split + ['two']*split + [3.0]*split + [None]*split + ['four']*split
hyp.plot(m, '.', hue=hue)"
findings.expected: Tutorial cells execute and produce the hue-colored scatter shown in the committed outputs (e.g. make the last chunk absorb the remainder: sizes = [n//5]*4 + [n - 4*(n//5)]; verified working, see w1_hue_fixed_legend.png).
findings.actual: ValueError: hue has 8120 entries but the data has 8124 observations; hue must have exactly one value (or one row, for a matrix hue) per observation.

findings.title: hyp.load('sotus') returns the NIPS topic-model Pipeline, not the documented State of the Union speeches (duplicate Google Drive id)
findings.description: EXAMPLE_DATA in hypertools/io/load.py maps 'sotus' and 'nips_model' to the SAME Google Drive id '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm' (lines 24 and 27). The hosted file behind that id is a CountVectorizer+LDA sklearn Pipeline: the cached ~/hypertools_data/sotus (downloaded Jul 2025) and ~/hypertools_data/nips_model (downloaded Jul 2026) are byte-identical (md5 6a350ab8d85db34e7b924ac8a7f2a19b), and unpickling emits sklearn InconsistentVersionWarning for CountVectorizer/LatentDirichletAllocation/Pipeline from version 1.0.2. Since 'sotus' does not end with '_model', load() returns the Pipeline as if it were data, and hyp.plot(hyp.load('sotus')) crashes. The load() docstring (line ~167) documents 'sotus' as 'a collection of State of the Union speeches from 1989-2018'. Inherited from master (same duplicate id there), so every hypertools version currently ships a broken 'sotus' dataset.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp
s = hyp.load('sotus')
print(type(s))
hyp.plot(s)"
findings.expected: load('sotus') returns the SOTU text data (list of speech strings / DataFrame) suitable for hyp.plot, as documented in the load() docstring and promised by plot.ipynb's text section.
findings.actual: print(type(s)) -> <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'>; hyp.plot(s) -> TypeError: Unsupported data type passed. Supported types: Numpy Array, Pandas DataFrame, String, List of strings, List of numbers

X = np.random.randn(60,10)
hyp.align([X, X+1], align='SRM')"

findings.title: DeprecationWarnings from plot() and align() are invisible in notebooks (stacklevel attributes them to internal frames); reduce() gets it right
findings.description: In the freshly-executed notebooks, reduce.ipynb cell 25's legacy-dict warning is attributed to the user's cell (ipykernel_.../...py:1) and therefore displayed, but plot.ipynb cell 23 (same legacy dict) and align.ipynb cell 16 (align='SRM') display no warning at all, even though both emit DeprecationWarning under warnings.simplefilter('always') (verified: plot emits it twice, align once). IPython's default filter only shows DeprecationWarnings attributed to __main__, so with the current stacklevel notebook users -- the tutorial audience -- never learn they are using deprecated forms.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import warnings, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.randn(60,10)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    hyp.plot(X, '.', reduce={'model':'PCA','params':{'whiten':True}})
    print([str(x.message)[:80] for x in w], [x.filename for x in w])"
findings.expected: Deprecation warnings raised with stacklevel pointing at the caller's frame so notebook/script users see them once (as reduce() does); also plot() should not emit the same warning twice per call.
findings.actual: Executed plot.ipynb cell 23 and align.ipynb cell 16 contain no warning output; warnings-capture shows plot emits DeprecationWarning twice with filenames inside hypertools internals rather than the user frame.

findings.title: legend=True with a hue containing None labels: None-group points are colored but omitted from the legend
findings.description: Fixing the tutorial's hue example to exact length (5 groups: 1, 'two', 3.0, None, 'four') and passing legend=True yields a plot with 5 distinct colors but a legend listing only 4 entries (1, two, 3.0, four). The None-group points (a full fifth of the data, rendered in their own color) are unidentifiable from the legend, which misrepresents the grouping. plot.ipynb explicitly advertises None as a valid hue entry and says the legend is 'generated based on your groupings'.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp
m = hyp.load('mushrooms'); n = m.shape[0]; b = n//5
sizes = [b]*4 + [n-4*b]
labels = [1,'two',3.0,None,'four']
hue = sum(([l]*s for l,s in zip(labels,sizes)), [])
fig = hyp.plot(m, '.', hue=hue, legend=True)
fig.savefig('hue_legend.png')"
findings.expected: Either a legend entry for the None group (e.g. 'None' / 'unlabeled') or a visually neutral (e.g. grey) rendering distinguishing unlabeled points from labeled groups.
findings.actual: Legend shows exactly: 1, two, 3.0, four -- while five colored groups are plotted (see evidence; blue cluster has no legend entry).

findings.title: reduce()'s unknown-model error message points at legacy docs, has embedded whitespace, and the wrong-key dict message recommends the deprecated 'params' spec
findings.description: hyp.reduce(X, reduce='NotAModel') raises 'ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce          for supported models' -- runs of literal spaces mid-sentence, no model names listed (align()'s equivalent message enumerates every supported name), and the link targets the pre-1.0 hypertools.tools.reduce API page (currently HTTP 200, but it documents the legacy API and the anchor will not describe 1.0's reduce). Worse, passing a dict with a wrong key yields 'pass ... a dictionary of custom params as the value of the "params" key' -- i.e. the error message instructs users to use exactly the legacy format that triggers a DeprecationWarning when followed.
findings.expected: Message enumerates supported model names (like align's does), no stray whitespace, links current docs, and recommends the canonical {'model','args','kwargs'} spec.
findings.actual: ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html... || ValueError: If passing a dictionary, pass the model as the value of the "model" key and a                 dictionary of custom params as the value of the "params" key.

findings.title: align.ipynb/analyze.ipynb say SRM is provided 'via the Brain Imaging Analysis Kit (brainiak)' -- it is vendored, brainiak is not a dependency
findings.description: align.ipynb cell 2 ('...option to use the Shared Response Model (SRM) for alignment, if preferred, via the Brain Imaging Analysis Kit (brainiak)') and analyze.ipynb cell 25 ("'SRM' - implements shared response model via Brainiak") imply hypertools calls the brainiak package. hypertools 1.0 vendors the implementation (hypertools/align/srm.py: 'Adapters over the vendored hypertools.external.brainiak.{SRM, DetSRM, RSRM}'); brainiak is not installed in the venv and is not required. Users may waste time installing brainiak (a notoriously heavy install) to use align='SRM'.
findings.repro: grep -n 'vendored' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/align/srm.py; /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import brainiak" # ModuleNotFoundError, yet align(..., model='SRM') works
findings.expected: Tutorials say SRM is bundled with hypertools (based on the brainiak implementation), no extra install needed.
findings.actual: hypertools/align/srm.py docstring: 'Adapters over the vendored hypertools.external.brainiak.{SRM, DetSRM, RSRM}.'; SRM alignment ran successfully in this audit with no brainiak package installed.

findings.title: normalize misuse raises AssertionError naming an internal parameter ('scale_type') instead of the user-facing kwarg
findings.description: hyp.plot(X, '.', normalize='banana') and hyp.analyze([X], normalize='banana') both raise 'AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' The message content is helpful, but (a) it names 'scale_type', a parameter the user never passed (they passed normalize=), and (b) it is an AssertionError, which disappears under python -O and is conventionally reserved for internal invariants, not input validation. Note the accepted values ('none' included) also slightly differ from the three options the plot/analyze tutorials list (across/within/row).
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.analyze([np.random.randn(20,5)], normalize='banana')"
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize must be one of 'across', 'within', 'row', 'none', or a fitted Normalizer (got 'banana').
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.
